text:
I have been psychologically short $NFLX for years and believe this year has vindicated that psychological short.

Unfortunately I was way too much of a chicken to actually short/buy puts 😂

In all seriousness, my bear case has always been that they cannot keep up content spend to justify their growth without massive hits. The massive hits have faded away which has significantly hurt the type of subscriber/adgrowth needed for the stock to expand from its premium multiple. 

YouTube’s algorithm was another bear case. How does Netflix compete with a creator economy that is growing rapidly without spending even more money? The move to buy Warner Bros, live sports, podcasting…all of it was to hide that they just don’t have the massive hits needed to keep growing. 

HOWEVER…at some point, the company becomes too cheap. Valuation is 5 year low and they are buying back a ton of stock. I genuinely don’t see how they get back to massive growth again without a MAJOR hit like Squid Games…all the ads/NFL/videogames/buybacks in the world won’t get the street excited without hits.

But I wonder if the margin of safety has finally gotten to the point where their most is being meaningfully discounted (I do think they have a large moat with huge barriers to entry) and if the stock price is officially reflecting that.

Are you buying the dip?

text:
AI-related borrowing is skyrocketing.

US Dollar-denominated AI-related corporate bond issuance is up to $419 billion so far in 2026, the highest annual figure on record.

This represents a +90% YoY increase from full-year 2025 and a +437% increase from full-year 2024.

Year-to-date, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon, $AMZN, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, and Oracle, $ORCL, have issued a combined $157 billion in corporate bonds, accounting for 37% of the total.

This is followed by investment-grade and high-yield data center and computing companies, which have raised $66 billion and $37 billion, respectively, and together account for ~25% of AI-related issuance.

Other AI-linked corporate bonds have represented $159 billion, or 38%.

The AI revolution is driving an unprecedented wave of corporate borrowing.

ko_summary: @munster_gene: 젠슨 황이 VW와 볼보가 메르세데스에 이어 Hyperion 고객이 됐다고 발표한 것은 $TSLA FSD에 호재. Hyperion은 턴키 솔루션이 아니며 전통 완성차는 여전히 데이터와 모델이 부족하다. 피지컬 AI는 $NVDA 매출의 5% 미만이지만 3분의 1이 될 수 있다.
text:
Good news for $TSLA FSD. Feels like autonomous driving is at an inflection point. 

Jensen reiterates that physical AI is the next big wave and announces VW and Volvo are joining Mercedes as Hyperion customers.

My take: Hyperion helps traditional automakers build autonomy, but it’s not a turnkey solution, they still lack the data and model. Traditional auto remains in a tight spot on autonomy.

Physical AI is a small part of Nvidia revenue today (sub 5%). Over time it could become a third. $NVDA

$NVDA is expanding AI computing into telecom networks as $TMUS completes world's first AI-RAN call on a live network with $NOK.

My take: I disagree with the blanket shift. Some will struggle ($CRM, $ADBE). Others—especially security and data monitoring software—should benefit as agents increase activity and complexity.

en_summary: @munster_gene: $NVDA announced DSX Pod, a bus sized containerized mini data center of Vera Rubins that can be linked, cutting data center spin up from about 4 to 5 months to a month and improving ROI.
ko_summary: @munster_gene: $NVDA가 Vera Rubin 클러스터를 담은 버스 크기의 컨테이너형 미니 데이터센터 DSX Pod를 발표. 연결 가능하며 데이터센터 구축 기간을 약 4~5개월에서 1개월로 줄여 ROI를 개선.
text:
$NVDA announces DSX Pod.  Basically a mini data center in a container the size of a bus. They can be connected.  Each one has cluster of Vera Rubins, connected and cooled. Little onsite assembly. 

Bottom line is it speeds up the  time that it takes to spin up a data center from around 4-5 months to a month. Less wasted idle compute. Makes the ROI more attractive.

name: Gene Munster

ko_summary: @munster_gene은 젠슨 황이 베를린 기조연설을 엔비디아는 GPU만이 아닌 AI 팩토리 회사라는 말로 시작했다고 전했다. 그는 이 점이 아직 저평가돼 있다며 소프트웨어, 라이브러리, 하드웨어가 전환 비용을 높이고 반복적인 업그레이드 주기를 뒷받침하는 풀스택을 이루므로 $NVDA 매출 성장에 장기적으로 긍정적이라고 봤다.
text:
Jensen opens Berlin keynote with the familiar line: Nvidia is an AI factory company, not just GPUs.

text: There is no question in my mind that there is circular financing going on today. But it occurred during the internet bubble as well. I think the more marginal neo-cloud players will have issues getting future financing but the stronger companies will be able to keep this going into 2027. Some of the biggest spenders, like $AMZN, $GOOGL, $MSFT, have the best balance sheets and massive other businesses to fund their AI investment and backstop debt for some of the neoclouds. Not to mention $NVDA and $AVGO that have massive cash flows to invest and backstop debt as well due to the above public cloud vendors buying their chips.

text:
Elon Musk says AI chips designed for space should "run hot" because raising operating temperatures by 20% in Kelvin could cut radiator mass in half significantly reducing the weight $SPCX needs to launch into orbit.

He also argues that trillion-parameter AI models can tolerate occasional radiation-induced bit flips potentially making orbital data centers easier to build without requiring same level of protection as traditional spacecraft electronics.
